lines.note: Hendo, katainaka, means a village or outlying district. Arrabaldes is divided across the next row.
Hendo hennai is another expression for these outlying settlements; the comparison point follows below.
The settlements are peripheral relative to Miyako, the capital. Miyaco is Japanese embedded in the Portuguese definition.
Hendou, henji ugoku, is change or variation. Mudanca restores the Portuguese noun lost in OCR Malanca.
Alteracao and perturbacao add disturbance or agitation to the sense of change. The missing letters were checked in the scan.
Hengai is failure to keep a promise. The repeated fengai in the example supports F rather than OCR B.
Yakusoku wo hengai suru is retracting or failing a promise. Promessa continues across the row boundary.
The gloss says not fulfilling the promise. Comprir is retained as the historical printed form, rather than modern cumprir.
Hengaye is an alternative form; Melius explicitly recommends hengai. That preference is the dictionary's, not an editorial modernization.
Henji in shukusan henji concerns a peripheral island or land. This example should not be confused with henji meaning a reply.

runs.text: comarcãa a algũa terra firme, & larga como

lines.note: The island lies near a large mainland. Terra firme, restored from OCR frme, is essential to the geographical comparison.

runs.text: Iapão em comparação da China. S.

lines.note: Japan relative to China is the stated example. S identifies the written register of this geographical expression.
Henge is transformation into another appearance or shape. Figura corrects a vowel error in the Portuguese gloss.
Henge no mono is a transformed being or thing; the visible no mono sequence is not OCR mo mono.

runs.text: como o Diabo em figura de rapoſa, &c.

lines.note: The missionary illustrates transformation with a devil in fox form. This expresses the source's framing, not a modern identification of all such beings.
Tengu kitsune ni henge suru means a tengu assuming fox form. Both kitsune and henge are supported by the gloss and scan.

runs.text: o demonio a figura de rapoſa.

lines.note: The Portuguese repeats that the demon takes the appearance of a fox, completing the transformation example.
Hengen, katakotoba, is an incomplete or brief utterance. Kotoba and Portuguese palavra jointly expose two OCR word corruptions.

runs.text: ta, ou qualquer palaurinha que pode dar no co-

lines.note: Even a small word can affect someone's heart. Palaurinha is the diminutive of palavra, not the separated OCR fragment.
Coracao de alguem completes that effect on another person's heart; it belongs to the same hengen definition.
Hen-i is change, glossed henji kawaru. The printed internal hyphen distinguishes the vowel after n and is not a line-end mark.
Completes variedade. The vowel sequence rie is restored from OCR ric without changing the physical line division.
Henji, kaeri koto, is a reply. Keep this reply entry distinct from the preceding change entry.
Fẽji / fenzuru means changing one's appearance or form. An enlarged view shows the contraction mark over e; the following example concerns changing into a mountain ascetic's costume.
The example concerns Hougan wearing a yamabushi's appearance. Vt introduces the example; it is not Portuguese Et.
Yamabushi no sugata ni henji means changing into an ascetic's guise before traveling through the northern provinces. Sugata corrects the OCR vowel.
Completes the honorific verb. The following source label remains Tog. pending identification; the Portuguese begins the account of Honguandono changing dress.

runs.text: trajos de Yamabuxi deceo pera as partes do

lines.note: Yamabuxi names the mountain ascetic whose dress is assumed; it is an embedded Japanese term, not the OCR split Yam ibuxi.
Norte completes the northern destination. Yakusoku wo fenzuru then introduces breaking a promise.
Quebrar a promessa completes that translation. Kokoro ga fenzuru introduces a change of mind or intention.
The Portuguese names will or purpose as what changes; iro wo begins the next example concerning facial color.
Iro wo fenzuru means changing the color of the face. Rosto belongs to Portuguese and its s-type is retained.
Henjou, kaeshi tatematsuru, is replying respectfully. The restored headword matches the honorific verb and the noble addressee below.
Pessoa nobre specifies the high-status addressee. The OCR double-l reading is incompatible with the printed s-types and noun.
Henjo is a written reply by letter, a separate noun from the preceding respectful action.

Fenjô is the illuminating sense of henjou, illustrated by Quǒ miô fenjǒ. The headword and example have visibly different o marks; they are retained rather than normalized to a single spelling of the Buddhist expression.
Fotoque is the illuminator in the Portuguese explanation: the Buddha illuminates all things. The embedded term is printed italic here.
Henman means filling everywhere, explained by amaneku michitari. Initial F, not B, is supported by both the scan and the example.
Kono sekai ni aku... begins 'in this world, evil...'. The ni particle was misread as mi; the Portuguese describes fullness or abundance.
Aku ga henman shite aru says evil pervades the world. Fenman repeats the headword rather than OCR tenman.
De maldade completes the world's being full of evil, with S marking written use.
Henmet is change and destruction, glossed kawari horobu. Final t represents a checked ending rather than a missing full syllable.
Destruicao completes the two-part definition of change and destruction; the written-register label follows.
Fenmocu concerns a dispute or troublesome affair. The crowded m was split into ni by OCR; NINJAL's headword identification supports returning to the visible m rather than inventing fennioku.

runs.text: raço, briga, &c. que ſe leuanta entre al-

lines.note: The entry includes quarrels arising between people; alguns continues across the row boundary.
Completes alguns and adds a second meaning, a book's table or index. Taboada restores the final vowel in OCR taboadu.
Fenmonai describes something of little consequence or profit. The enlarged scan and the NINJAL headword agree on one n before m; the first-pass double-n guess has been removed.
Proveito completes 'of little importance and benefit'. This short continuation belongs to the preceding adjective.
Henni, katamimi, is one ear. The Portuguese ouvidos is divided across the next row.
Henni ni shite rihi wo tadasu begins a maxim about judging right and wrong from one-sided hearing. Ri-hi is not OCR ri-fi.
Koto kanawazu makes that judgment impossible. The Portuguese begins hearing with only one ear.

runs.text: orelha não ſe pode julgar, & diſcernir o bem

lines.note: One cannot judge or distinguish good by hearing only one side; the paired evil follows below.
E o mal completes the good/evil contrast. S identifies the maxim as written usage.
Hennou, kaeshi osamuru, means returning or paying what is owed. The final payment recipient follows in the gloss.
The debt is repaid particularly to one's lord. Preserve the historical printed adverb rather than silently regularizing it.
Henoko is anatomically glossed as the sac of the testicles, the scrotum; the definition is narrower than some later uses of the word.
Henpou is recompense, kaeshi mukuu, covering repayment of good actions as well as the retaliation below.

runs.text: & vingança de males, poſto que mais propri-

lines.note: The gloss adds vengeance for wrongs, then narrows the usual sense in the following row.
The dictionary says the term more properly means revenge. Henpou wo suru starts across the row break.
Henpou wo suru is taking revenge. A Christian example then begins on aruji Deus, with Deus split between rows.
God is said to recompense good and evil, using the honorific nasaseraruru. Deus and Christao elsewhere are borrowed Christian vocabulary inside Japanese examples.

runs.text: Deus N. ſenhor da o pago dos bẽs, & males.

lines.note: The Portuguese translates God our Lord giving recompense for good and evil; retain the source's theological claim as a gloss.
Henpokkai denotes the entire world. Do not infer an unprinted space or repair its gemination solely from a modern compound analysis.
Henpuku is bat, explained by koumuri. The printed form lacks the t of modern koumori-related alternatives and is retained.
The homophone henpuku means overturning, kaeshi kutsugaeru. Caindo is physically divided in the Portuguese gloss.
Completes falling or capsizing. This is the overturning entry, not a continuation of the bat definition.

runs.text: Contradizer a algũa couſaa que hum

lines.note: Henki is opposition to something one dislikes. The nasal vowel in algua was corrupted by OCR; the broader phrase continues below.

runs.text: tẽ aſco, ou auerſão, por obras ou palauras. Vt,

lines.note: Aversion may be expressed by acts or words. The abbreviated tem is tẽ, not grave-accented te.

Varui gẽtioxù describes hostile gentios, with a Japanese shuu ending, rejecting Christian teaching. The t is badly damaged and is supplied contextually in this working reading; the visible loan-word sequence and the next line's Portuguese gentios support it, but this remains a useful human-check point.

runs.text: Os gentios maos des danhão da doc-

lines.note: The Japanese suru completes the example; the Portuguese begins the account of hostile gentiles scorning the doctrine.

runs.text: trina dos chriſtãos, & moſtranlhe pouca von-

lines.note: Christaos identifies the Christians whose doctrine is rejected. The gloss continues with showing it little goodwill.
Completes vontade and the conventional etcetera abbreviation; OCR e with an accent was not a lexical word.
Henrei, reigaeshi, is returning a visit or gift. The Portuguese paga here concerns reciprocity rather than necessarily money.
Retorno dalgum presente completes the reciprocal-gift sense of henrei.
Hensai, hotori/kiwa, is an edge or limit. The headword begins with F, matching its repetition below.
Hensai mo nai and kagiri mo nai both express having no limit. Nao starts the Portuguese negative construction.
Ter termo nem fim completes 'have neither limit nor end', matching both Japanese examples.

runs.text: O peregrinar por diuerſas partes, ou

lines.note: Hensan is pilgrimage through different places, not simply casual travel in this religiously framed definition.

runs.text: andar de terra ẽ terra fazẽdo certos exercicios

lines.note: The traveler goes from place to place performing particular exercises or observances, whose practitioners are named next.

runs.text: como fazem os Bõzos chamados Yẽgueſos.

lines.note: Yenguesos is the source's name for those practitioners; the Portuguese plural ending is retained. It is an embedded Japanese-derived term.

runs.text: Bõzos que andão desta maneira pe-

lines.note: Hensanzou denotes monks who travel in this way. Peregrinando continues across the physical row boundary.
Completes peregrinando, closing the description of the traveling monks.
Hensat is a reply letter, with a checked final t. Gohensat ni begins the respectful example acknowledging such a reply.

runs.text: Recebi a carta de voſſa mer-

lines.note: Azukari soro completes the receipt formula. The Portuguese says receiving the addressee's letter.

runs.text: ce em reposta da minha. S.

lines.note: The received letter answers the speaker's own letter; S marks the epistolary written register.
Hentou is a reply, equated with henji. The following example repeats hentou before the verb on the next row.
Yuu completes hentou yuu, to answer. The vowel mark is a length mark rather than OCR's nasal tilde.
Henshi, katatoki, is a short interval, su koshi no aida. Initial P was an OCR error for F.
Fenximo nǒ means without even a moment's delay. The enlarged image supports the separate negative nǒ after mo, not the OCR's extra a; the Portuguese logo / sem tardança confirms the immediate sense.
Logo ou sem tardanca explicitly means immediately, without delay, supporting the preceding example's negative-time interpretation.
Henshin, kaeshi mairasuru, is respectfully returning a borrowed object. The Portuguese says paying back what was taken.

runs.text: ſe tomou ẽprestado particularmente ao ſenhor,

lines.note: The borrowed object is returned particularly to a lord; the nasal abbreviation in emprestado is retained rather than expanded.

runs.text: ou a outra peſſoa honrada, ou do meſmo teor.

lines.note: The recipient may instead be another honored person or someone of equivalent standing; this clause ends before the next qualification.

runs.text: Não ſe dirà de arroz, dinheiro, &c. mas de

lines.note: The word is not used for rice or money. Nao se dira supplies that restriction, correcting garbled OCR dtrade.

runs.text: couſas que ſe tornão as meſmas numero como de

lines.note: It concerns returning the very same objects, not equivalent quantities. The sentence continues onto the next page with an example.
